title: R’ Yose of Malchaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Vayikra Rabbah פ״ג־רב and פדר״ב 31a for the teaching that he and R’ Yehoshua of Sikhnin give in R’ Levi’s name. The matching passages are Vayikra Rabbah 26:2 and Pesikta DeRav Kahana 4:2 in the consulted editions.

In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:5 he says of Rav Huna’s words, “His force is greater in two respects”; in Avodah Zarah 2:4 he asks R’ Mana. Hyman identifies him as the first Mana: in אב״ר1:36 [the earlier compared Eichah Rabbah passage is at 1:37], when R’ Yose of Malchaya died, R’ Yochanan and Resh Lakish went up to perform a kindness for him, and R’ Yitzchak Paskaa went with them. Hyman argues: if so, he died before Resh Lakish, whereas the second Mana had not known R’ Yochanan and Resh Lakish.

notes.text: The supplied work and locator forms פדר״ב, פ״ג־רב and אב״ר 1:36 remain difficult. The matching funeral account is in Eichah Rabbah 1:37. The checked Kiddushin passage explicitly supplies Rav Huna, while Hyman’s two-Manas chronology remains his inference.

No new primary scalar was returned. Yose and Yehoshua of Sikhnin are TWO reporters in Levi’s name, not two names for one person. Hyman identifies the first Mana through the funeral and argues IF SO that Yose died before Resh Lakish; the second Mana’s acquaintance claim is his argument. Earlier Eichah1:37 comparison remains beside supplied אב״ר1:36, without proof of a siglum’s printing history. פ״ג־רב and פדר״ב remain visible and unresolved; the latter is not automatically Pesikta de-Rav Kahana. Rav Huna is inherited contextual expansion of ר״ה, not a newly inspected occurrence. Malchaya follows the supplied place form, without harmonizing Magdlayya or binding identity.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. II, p. 741) appears to cite Vayikra Rabbah 26:2. The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 26:2 and Pesikta DeRav Kahana 4:2 both give the teaching in R’ Levi’s name with Yose and Yehoshua of Sikhnin named as two transmitters. The precise historical pagination of the Pesikta citation has not been collated. In the printed funeral citation the work appears as איכ״ר and the section as 1:36. The corresponding funeral at Eichah Rabbah 1:37 names Yochanan, Resh Lakish and Yitzchak Psaka. Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:4 records Yose bringing a case before Mana. The identification of this Mana with the first Mana and the resulting chronology are Hyman’s inferences.
